Answer: C
Reason: The radiograph shows a well-defined, ovoid soft-tissue mass in the right paracardiac region; combined with the chronic 10-month history of discomfort in a young woman, this presentation is most characteristic of unicentric Castleman disease (hyaline vascular type), which typically manifests as a solitary, slow-growing mediastinal or paracardiac mass. Pericardial cysts are usually asymptomatic and water-density, while lipomas would appear radiolucent, and pneumonia would present acutely with ill-defined consolidation.
